quotes.text: This page is a general guide for Stripe users, not a comprehensive reference for card network monitoring programs.
In some cases, if you issued a full refund before a dispute, you can respond to the dispute.
Visa’s data is used to determine your compliance status each month and is reported with a one-month delay.
Effective October 2026, the Visa Merchant Elevated Risk Program (MERP) applies to businesses that accept Visa payments in the Asia Pacific region.
Visa evaluates these signals together rather than against individual thresholds, and doesn’t publish the thresholds it uses.

old_evidence.text: In some cases, if you issued a full refund at least 10 days before a dispute, we can ask to have the dispute removed from the account.
Accounts can view Stripe’s estimates of their VAMP metrics in their [VAMP dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/test/radar/cbmp/vamp).
These estimates might differ from Visa’s final VAMP numbers.

findings: The November guide adds Visa's Merchant Elevated Risk Program, effective October 2026 for businesses accepting Visa in Asia Pacific (new lines 140-164). MERP assesses early-life concentrated risk using transaction/fraud/non-fraud dispute/authorization/decline signals together, without published numeric identification thresholds. If confirmed, possible consequences include network assessments that might be passed on, backdated fraud disputes, remediation, Stripe account closure under some circumstances, and potential VMSS listing. These are conditional outcomes, not proof this account was identified or charged.

The current source summary and stripe-dispute-monitoring-programs concept enumerate VAMP/VSEFP, Mastercard programs and AusPayNet only (source lines 11-13, 22-110; concept lines 19-89). Without MERP, an Asia Pacific early-risk query could select the wrong Visa program or look for a numeric threshold where the new capture says none is published. This merits a new dated section or clear route in the source and concept.

The VAMP dashboard section changes from May's test-mode URL and History/Historical-current/Projected status panels (old lines 127-135) to a non-test URL with Program standing, trend, Visa data, Stripe data and Resources (new lines 128-138). Visa's monthly data determines compliance and arrives one month later; Stripe's daily computation is an estimate that may differ. The current source line 45's generic estimated-metrics label should distinguish these data authorities.

The refund passage changes materially: May said Stripe could ask to remove a dispute after a full refund at least 10 days before it (old line 22), while November says that after a full refund before a dispute one can respond to the dispute and links further guidance (new line 23). Do not carry the old 10-day removal request forward as a current network guarantee, and do not infer it was abolished solely because omitted. Both captures say refunds and dispute outcomes generally do not determine network-monitoring counts (old lines 22-30; new lines 23-31).

The VAMP count/ratio/volume and enumeration thresholds, VSEFP, Mastercard ECM/HECM/EFM thresholds and fine schedules, and AusPayNet FMP rules remain substantially the same (old lines 77-325; new lines 78-353), aside from table rendering and the inserted MERP/dashboard material. The document explicitly says it is a general guide rather than comprehensive or authoritative up-to-date network documentation (old line 16; new line 17); current source line 13's 'Comprehensive reference' overstates that boundary.
substantive_changes: New October 2026 Visa MERP for Asia Pacific, with unpublished holistic identification thresholds, short response window, conditional assessments/backdated disputes/remediation/account closure/VMSS listing (new lines 140-164).
VAMP Dashboard now separates Visa monthly authoritative data from Stripe daily estimates and uses revised panels and URL (old lines 127-135; new lines 128-138).
Refund-before-dispute guidance changes from an at-least-10-day removal-request possibility to a response route without that timing statement (old line 22; new line 23).
historical_claims_to_preserve: May's at-least-10-days refund-removal wording is historical only; both captures maintain that refunds and wins/losses generally do not determine network-monitoring dispute counts (old lines 22-30; new lines 23-31).
VAMP disputes/fraud and enumeration tracks remain separate; captured regional count/ratio/volume thresholds and TC15/TC40 counting caveats persist (old lines 77-125; new lines 78-126).

VSEFP is limited to the specified US domestic 3DS context, Mastercard rate denominator uses prior-month captured payments, and AusPayNet FMP tracks qualifying Australian CNP fraud quarterly (old lines 137-268; new lines 166-296).

Network monitoring may include disputes hidden from Stripe Dashboard/API and can differ from Stripe's own rate estimates; program outcomes can threaten card-processing ability (old lines 10-38; new lines 11-39).
conflicts: Current source line 13 calls the page comprehensive despite the raw's explicit general-guide, not-comprehensive notice (old line 16; new line 17).
Current source and concept omit Visa MERP, a distinct new program for Asia Pacific businesses with unpublished thresholds and conditional severe outcomes (new lines 140-164).
Current source line 45 describes VAMP dashboard as estimated metrics only; new lines 134-137 distinguish Visa-sourced compliance data from Stripe estimates and a one-month reporting lag.

Current source line 17's 'Refunds don't help' shorthand should not erase the new response route after a pre-dispute full refund; network monitoring still counts disputes and the May removal-request sentence cannot be assumed current (old line 22; new line 23).
unresolved_questions: Visa MERP's exact identification thresholds are not published in this capture; no account-level inclusion, assessment, closure or VMSS listing is established.
The new page does not settle whether Stripe can still request removal under the old 10-day full-refund scenario; it states a different response route and links further guidance.
The captured monitoring numbers and timelines are Stripe's dated general guide, not independent up-to-date card-network authority or this merchant's compliance status.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/monitoring-programs, the November capture adds Visa MERP for Asia Pacific from October 2026, with unpublished holistic thresholds and potentially serious conditional outcomes (new lines 140-164). [[source-stripe-disputes-monitoring-programs]] and its concept currently omit it. The VAMP dashboard also now distinguishes Visa monthly compliance data from Stripe daily estimates (new lines 128-138 versus old lines 127-135). May's full-refund-at-least-10-days removal-request statement at old line 22 is replaced by a dispute-response route at new line 23.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/disputes/monitoring-programs, [[source-stripe-disputes-monitoring-programs]] should add MERP without inventing numeric thresholds or treating possible assessments, backdated disputes, account closure or VMSS listing as inevitable (new lines 142-158). Preserve the dated VAMP, Mastercard and AusPayNet calculations from old lines 77-325 and new lines 78-353, plus the notice that this is a general guide (old line 16; new line 17). Clarify that Visa monthly reports determine VAMP compliance while Stripe's daily numbers are estimates (new lines 134-137).
